problems.note: The narration says only "Part of the pizza is shaded" and gives no slice count or shading. The answer (1/3) depends entirely on seeing a 3-slice circle with 1 shaded, so a child playing by sound cannot answer. Add the count to the narration, e.g. "A pizza is cut into 3 equal slices and 1 is shaded."

The narration says "This pizza is cut into equal slices" but never says how many. The answer (6) can only be found by counting the picture, so it cannot be answered by ear. State the count in the narration, or make the item depend on something the child hears.

The narration asks "How many sixths are shaded?" but does not say how many slices are shaded. The answer (2) depends only on the picture. Say the shaded amount in the narration, e.g. "Two of the six slices are shaded."

The choices are pictures, and the question "Which picture shows..." is answered by the picture. The spoken labels (1/3 of the circle, etc.) let a child match by name, so the item is still playable. Consider wording it around the labels only. The marked answer 1/3 (3 parts, 1 shaded) is correct.

The narration says to "cut the same pizza into 3 equal slices instead," but the picture still shows the 6-slice pizza. The answer (1) is correct, but the child is told to imagine a re-cut that the picture does not show. Reword, e.g. "Two sixths are shaded. How many thirds is that same amount?"

Step 5 says two sixths equals one third, but its picture shows only the 1/3 circle. The comparison is not visible. Consider showing the 2/6 circle beside it. Step 6's 4/6 picture is fine. Also, equivalence of thirds and sixths may be a Grade 3 expectation in the Ontario curriculum; confirm it fits the Grade 2 skill.

output.notes: I checked every marked answer and all are mathematically correct: tap-1 (1/3), keypad-1 (6), number-line-1 (3), tap-2 (1/3 picture), keypad-2 (2), tap-3 (2/6), keypad-3 (2), number-line-2 (4, VERIFY), tap-4 (No, VERIFY), keypad-4 (1), tap-5 (2/3), number-line-3 (2), keypad-5 (6), tap-6 (same amount, VERIFY), number-line-4 (4). The main issue is audio-only playability: three items (tap-1, keypad-1, keypad-2) have their answers only in the picture, and the narration does not say the counts. The rest of the items state their numbers in the narration, so they can be answered by sound.
